title: Florida Commuter Airlines Flight 65

agencies.name: National Transportation Safety Board
agencies.report_title: Florida Commuter Airlines, Inc., Douglas DC-3A

location.name: West End Settlement, Grand Bahama Island

summary: Douglas DC-3 crashed in Atlantic Ocean with 34 occupants when unrecovered wreckage and lack of flight recorders precluded determining probable cause; contributing factors included pitot blockage from mud dauber nests, pitot-static system discrepancies, thunderstorm activity, and inadequate airline management oversight.
probable_cause: Probable cause could not be determined due to unrecovered wreckage and no flight recorders. Contributing factors: thunderstorm activities, pitot-static system discrepancies, and lack of operational control by management.

factors.evidence: Pitot tubes left uncovered for five weeks with mud dauber nests blocking openings; improper maintenance procedure used to clear blockage (p. 19)
Preexisting discrepancies in pitot-static system affecting reliability of flight instruments (p. 19)
Chief mechanic used screwdriver and coat hanger instead of proper procedure to clear blockage (p. 19)
Known thunderstorm activities and turbulence in the area (p. 19)
Replacement pilot believed flight was Part 91, not required to have 6-month currency check (p. 19)
Lack of operational control exercised by airline management (p. 19)

events.text: Flight 65 attempted departure but aborted due to no airspeed indication
Maintenance determined mud dauber nests blocking pitot tube openings
Flight 65 departed West Palm Beach after reboarding
Flight 65 flew beyond range of Miami radar
Flight 65 made contact with approach controllers at Freeport
Approach cleared Flight 65 to descend to 1400 feet, last communication
Control tower tried to radio plane without response

recommendations.text: Require all aircraft in revenue passenger operations to have approved weather detection device for flight under IFR or night VFR when thunderstorms are expected

notes: Findings and Probable Cause sections read
Wreckage not recovered; no flight recorders installed
Probable cause unable to be determined; contributing factors extracted from report
